scope: Singapore medical discovery — Duke-NUS Medical School

verifiedFacts.claim: Duke-NUS offers a four-year graduate-entry MD jointly awarded by Duke University and the National University of Singapore; its curriculum includes core clinical clerkships, a research-and-scholarship period, and advanced clinical rotations.

The MD admissions requirements require a completed or final-year bachelor or honours degree, GAMSAT or MCAT results, and three to five references; applicants already holding MBBS or equivalent are not eligible.
Applicants from non-English-speaking curricula must submit TOEFL or IELTS evidence; the stated minimums include IELTS overall 7.0 and TOEFL iBT 5 for exams on or after 21 January 2026.

For the 2026-2027 MD intake, Duke-NUS lists annual tuition of SGD 50,050 for Singapore citizens, SGD 68,150 for permanent residents, and SGD 99,900 for international students; its FAQ also states that scholarships, bursaries and loans are available.

Singapore's Ministry of Health states that students accepted into Duke-NUS must sign the Government medical/dental Tuition Grant Agreement, and its First Schedule lists the Doctor of Medicine of Duke-NUS Graduate Medical School Singapore as a Singapore degree.
Duke-NUS says students must meet screening and immunisation requirements before matriculation because clinical training is mostly held in healthcare institutions.

holdReasons: Duke-NUS is a distinct graduate-entry school but its jointly awarded NUS degree requires careful treatment alongside the existing National University of Singapore catalog payload; no duplicate payload was created.
A publication decision needs an explicit editorial determination on representing this graduate-entry school separately from its existing NUS parent-university entry.
